messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: [Severity: P1] GPU pool gpunorth-1 effective capacity < 30% (queue depth 860). Trigger: queue_growth_rate > 200/min for 5m. Pager: @jordan_oncall @mike_sre

jordan_oncall: ack — looking now. any customer-facing impact?

incident-bot: symptoms: 502s and queued requests. Telemetry: token-serving-latency p95 1.8s -> 4.2s, errors 5xx 12%

samira_eng: i'm on driver/runtime. quick glance shows repeated CUDA/Xid 31 + process OOM on 3 nodes: gpun-3, gpun-5, gpun-8. hypothesis: recent kernel/driver rollout (rtn-2026-03-10) + burst traffic + heavy kv-cache usage.

mike_sre: checking autoscaler state — looks like cluster autoscaler attempted new nodes but EC2/GPU quota blocked launches; k8s failed to attach NVMe volumes on the new nodes before timeouts.

eva_support: seeing multiple customer tickets for embeddings timeouts, flagged priority. i've DM'd sales for top 3 enterprise accounts.

jordan_oncall: Plan: 1) shift traffic to fallback pool (gpubackup/us-east) 2) cordon + drain affected nodes 3) if driver continues failing, rollback kernel/driver. objections?

samira_eng: agree. immediate mitigations: a) drain gpun-3/5/8 gracefully (300s) b) route requests to gpubackup with weight-based policy c) if Xid persists after drains, roll driver back to 510.3 kernel module.

mike_sre: autoscaler is hitting per-org GPU quota in this region. raising burst on dedicated-reserve (preemptible) to accept queued work while we stabilize.

jordan_oncall: executing drains now.

jordan_oncall: running:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpun-3
kubectl drain gpun-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=300
/opt/tools/route-requests --from-pool gpunorth-1 --to-pool gpubackup --weight 0.5
```

deploy-bot: Routing change applied: 50% -> gpubackup. 12% of requests rerouted initially for canary.

samira_eng: watching dmesg on gpun-5: 
```text
[12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=2345, GPU(0000:65:00): PID 2345(serve) was killed
[12345.679002] oom_kill: invoked for process 2345 (serve)
[12345.679101] nvkm_gpu: destroyed context...
```

mike_sre: autoscaler logs: attempted_scale_up=5, successful=0, reason="quota_exceeded". spun up +12 preemptible nodes in dedicated-reserve as fallback.

jordan_oncall: metrics update: p95 latency improved 4.2s -> 2.1s, queue depth 860 -> 220, 5xx errors down to 6%.

eva_support: status page updated and top customers notified. will keep them informed.

samira_eng: note: continuing to see occasional Xid 31 on gpun-8 after drain; looks like memory corruption under long-lived batching. not ready to roll driver unless it recurs post-drain. rollback estimate 18-30m including validation.

ana_prod: can we deprioritize non-critical workloads? suggest throttling background batch/low-tier to 10% token rate.

mike_sre: applying rate limit config for low-tier traffic now (token bucket reduced).

jordan_oncall: handoff plan: staying for 25m and then handing to @mike_sre. live status: partial recovery, queue decreasing, affected nodes drained, failover pool active. watch for repeat Xid events.

mike_sre: ack, i'll take the night watch. created incident page: https://redwood.status/incident/1999012345 — adding metrics graphs and node traces.

ops-bot: Reminder: create post-incident RCA ticket and tag eng-ml + eng-runtime.

samira_eng: adding logs and a short timeline to the incident doc. suspected root cause: driver/kernel incompatibility exacerbated by memory fragmentation from continuous batching; autoscaler unable to replace failing nodes due to quota leading to temporary capacity exhaustion and queue growth.

jordan_oncall: :thumbsup: good coordination. If stable in 1h, we'll close and move to RCA + customer communication. handoff_ts=1999012420

mike_sre: taking over. final quick check before I go fully async: p95 1.9s, errors 2.3%, queue 45. will escalate immediately if regressions.
